subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a governed durable conversational rule layer and all-explicitly-mentioned-bots reply contract, or keep current memory/mention behavior and handle only the narrower Feishu bugs?
rationale: The request changes memory authority, conflict precedence, durable storage/API shape, and multi-agent channel reply semantics; source inspection shows adjacent mechanisms but no existing product contract that automation can safely fill in.

options.title: Design the rule and mention contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines authority precedence, promotion review, supersession, storage, plugin/API boundaries, and per-channel reply semantics before code work.

options.title: Split to narrow Feishu bugs only
options.body: Treat durable rule learning as out of scope for now and focus implementation on the existing Feishu mention-loss issues linked from this issue.

options.title: Reject durable rule learning for core
options.body: Close the broad rule-learning direction as not planned and ask for plugin or ClawHub experiments unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design the rule and mention contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines authority precedence, promotion review, supersession, storage, plugin/API boundaries, and per-channel reply semantics before code work.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans memory, plugin/API boundaries, and product guardrails, and steipete has the strongest sampled history across those areas.
